the functionality of wheat flour is affected by the presence of cell wall components and can be manipulated by using enzymes, oxidants and antioxidants.
the detrimental effects of insoluable cell walls can be compensated by endoxylanases, and that the effects of water-extractable cell wall arabinoxylans can be prevented by ferulic acid.

the effects of cell wall components, especially arabinoxylans, on the functionality of gluten and the gas cell structure in bread dough.

cell wall materials, in particular water-unextractable arabinxylans, are detrimental to the functionality of wheat flour.

the effects of insoluble arabinoxylans and water-unextractable arabinxylans on the rheology and functionality of wheat doughs can be counteracted by the addition of water-soluble arabinoxylins and ferulic acid.
